messages:
Alex: Heads-up — p99 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate is lower than p95 for the last hour. Looks wrong, anyone else seeing this?
Maya: yup saw that earlier :eyes: — thought it was a UI quirk but it persists across time windows
Priya: can you paste a screenshot or paste the numbers? p95 and p99 values?
Alex: screenshot attached in thread (omitted). Quick numbers: p50=120ms, p95=512ms, p99=488ms in the 1h panel. Sample count ~14k.
Sam: that pattern usually means we're merging per-shard percentiles incorrectly. If we compute quantiles per-host then take a global quantile across hosts it can produce non-monotonic results.
Maya: agree. Our metric pipeline uses per-instance hdr histograms + we store summaries in telemetry DB. If the UI is pulling the stored per-host 99th then computing another quantile on top, that could break ordering.
Priya: can someone run a raw aggregation? e.g. PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{endpoint="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))` vs what the dashboard currently does.
Sam: I'll run the prom query now. If the prom-derived p99 > p95 then it's definitely an aggregation bug in the frontend.
ops-bot: Alert: rolling update of telemetry-workers started on infra-canary-3 — may affect metrics ingest for ~2m.
Maya: thanks for the heads-up. Ops canary might explain partial inconsistency, but non-monotonic percentiles are a logic bug, not transient.
Sam: ran the query: prom p95=525ms, p99=610ms (5m window). So raw data is fine. The dashboard service returns p99=488ms.
Priya: ok that pins it to the dashboard or its cache. I suspect we have two different percentile methods: t-digest for long-term and bucketed aggregations for real-time, and the UI mixes them.
Alex: is the UI doing timezone/window alignment or downsampling that could bias the numbers?
Sam: UI uses downsampling to 1-point-per-minute for 1h panel then recomputes percentiles client-side from downsampled points — that's the culprit. When you downsample summaries and then compute quantiles from the compressed points you can violate monotonicity.
Priya: action items: 1) stop client-side recompute of percentiles for histograms, 2) display sample_count next to each percentile, 3) add a tooltip explaining percentile method and time-window. I'll open a bug.
Maya: +1, also add an endpoint breakdown view so we can see per-backend contribution (model-serving vs router vs proxy). That will help diagnose cross-component tails.
Sam: quick patch idea: fetch raw bucket sums from backend for the visible time-range and compute histogram_quantile server-side, fall back to previous behavior if raw not available. Low-risk and fixes correctness.
Alex: sounds good. Priya can you own the ticket and set severity P2? This is misleading dashboards for customers.
Priya: will do. Creating issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1246 — notes: reproduce with /v1/generate, sample-counts, prom vs dashboard mismatch, proposed server-side quantile fix.
deploy-bot: Deployed telemetry-fix/patch-20240321 to staging (build d31c9).
Maya: I'll validate staging chart after the deploy. If staging looks good let's schedule a prod deploy tomorrow morning.
Alex: nice. Also can we add a regression test around percentile monotonicity in our dashboard E2E? Simple assert: p50 <= p95 <= p99 for all endpoints in smoke tests.
Sam: will add test.
Priya: added checklist in the ticket: backfill historical windows, add sample_count + percentile_method to telemetry payload, server-side quantile endpoint, UI change to prefer server quantiles.
Maya: thanks — looping in SRE to watch for any telemetry pipeline errors during the fix.
Alex: great, thanks team. Assigning reviewers: @Sam, @Maya. Will follow up with before/after screenshots. :thumbsup:
